tasks.title: Find why checkout p95 doubled after 2.14
tasks.problem:
Since: release 2.14, Nov 2 14:05
Latency: checkout p95 **820 ms → 1.7 s**
Timeouts: **0.9%** of payment attempts
Customers: charged without an order (support reports)
goal: Say what to change to get p95 back to the pre-2.14 level

context.title: Checkout latency dashboard, Oct 26 – Nov 4
context.note: p95 jumps at 14:05 on Nov 2, the deploy time of 2.14.

context.title: Pod logs during the peak, 2026-11-03 19:00–19:30
context.note: 3,140 × `EMFILE: too many open files`, all from the payments client.

inferences.text: The regression starts exactly with the 2.14 deploy, so it is caused by a change inside 2.14, not by traffic.
The payments client opens a new socket per retry and never caps them; under retries the pod runs out of file descriptors.
Double charges happen when the provider accepts a payment but our side times out before writing the order.

assumptions.text: The provider itself was healthy during the incident.
assumptions.why: Their status page shows no incident, but we have no provider-side metrics.
assumptions.verify: Ask the provider for request logs for Nov 3, 19:00–19:30.

result.summary:
Root cause: unbounded connections in payments client 4.0
Confirmed by: load test at 3× peak

items.text: Cap the pool at 50 connections per pod and add jittered backoff.
Load test with the cap: no `EMFILE` errors at 3× peak traffic.
p95 in the load test with the cap (was 1.7 s)

stages.title: Confirm the regression
stages.detail: Compared p95 per hour for two weeks around the release.

stages.title: Diff the release
stages.detail: Listed every dependency and config change in 2.14.

stages.title: Read the error logs
stages.detail: Grouped errors during the evening peak by message and source.

stages.title: Check the client changelog
stages.outcome: Pool limit default changed to unlimited.

stages.title: Reproduce under load
stages.detail: Ran the checkout load test with and without a pool cap.
stages.outcome: Cap removes the errors and restores latency.

stages.title: Write it up
stages.detail: Root cause, evidence and the proposed fix in the issue.
stages.outcome: Handed over to the fix task.

actions.why: Only an account owner can open a ticket with the provider; it confirms the one open assumption.

tasks.brief:
Cause: client 4.0 dropped the connection limit
Proven by: load test

tasks.title: Cap connections in the payments client
tasks.problem: Payments client opens **unlimited sockets** → file descriptors run out under retries.

inferences.text: 50 connections per pod covers peak with 2× headroom: peak is ~22 concurrent payment calls per pod.

assumptions.text: Idempotency keys are already sent on every retry, so backoff cannot create duplicate charges.
assumptions.why: The code path sets the key, but I did not see it in provider logs.
assumptions.verify: Check one retried request in the provider dashboard for the same idempotency key.

result.summary:
PR **#1290** ready:
- pool cap
- jittered exponential backoff
- pool saturation metric

items.text: Backoff 100 ms → 1.6 s with full jitter, 4 attempts max.
Unit tests pass; the load test from ACME-412 passes with this branch.

stages.title: Pick limits
stages.detail: Derived the pool size from peak concurrency.

stages.title: Implement cap and backoff
stages.detail: Configured the pool; wrapped retries in a backoff helper.

stages.title: Test
stages.detail: Unit tests and the incident load test.

approvals.text: Merge PR #1290 and ship it as 2.14.1 today.
approvals.why: Every evening peak until then repeats the incident.
